text.p: Lithuanian newspapers carried the following reports in their Tuesday editions. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy:

- Lithuanian President Algirdas Brazauskas vetoed the decision of the new parliament to form the board of National Radio and Television out of representatives from 13 public and artistic organisations.
- Prime Minister Gediminas Vagnorius has suggested a new tax police to control tax collection.
- The average interest rate for three-month government T-bills was still below 10 percent at auction on Monday although it was higher than last week.
- Reports that Birzai Diary intends to issue 24 million litas of shares abroad has sharply raised demand in Lithuania.
- All the biggest parliamentary parties were positive about Vagnorius' government programme and it is expected to be supported during today's parliament vote on it.
- A police patrol car hit three boys on a pedestrian crossing in Vilnius.
- The securities' commission registered on Friday the new share issue of Hermis bank. The share capital was boosted to 67 million litas.

- Outgoing prime minister Mindaugas Stankevicius said during his last press conference that GDP growth in the country was four percent this year and that foreign loans were estimated at some 15 percent of GDP. Stankevicius said the forecasts for GDP growth in the new government's plans were "very optimistic".
- Only 11 percent of Lithuanians consider that goods produced domestically are of high quality.
- Experts predict that the prices for residential real estate will go down in 1997.
